validity.recommendation: Keep as an existing, correctly classified operating gas transmission trunk line. Do NOT conflate with the OLDER, separate Okha-Komsomolsk OIL pipeline (1940s-built, twin 325mm+529mm-OD line, 624 km, largely closed) that shares nearly the same name and corridor.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION confirmed independent of GEM/gem.wiki. This PID is a real 1987-commissioned, 445 km / 720 mm OD natural-gas trunkline (OGJ 1995-05-15, ogj.com/home/article/17216636) running Okha (Sakhalin) to Komsomolsk-on-Amur (Khabarovsk Krai), still actively described as carrying gas as recently as 2026-04-24 (see fills[] Status). CAVEAT FOR FUTURE RESEARCHERS: the gem.wiki citation list harvested for this PID (wiki_citations.json) includes energybase.ru/pipeline/oha-komsomolsk-na-amure. That page was fetched and read directly: it describes a DIFFERENT, OLDER pipeline — a twin-line OIL pipeline (325 mm + 529 mm OD, 624 km, 5.5 MPa, 3.5 million mt/y, largely built 1940s/rebuilt 1962/1970) that runs the SAME Okha-Komsomolsk corridor but is NOT this gas line. This is independently corroborated by OGJ's 1995 article, which explicitly states: 'The gas pipeline route coincides with the route of the oil pipeline Okha-Komsomolsk except its Sakhalin section' and gives SEPARATE specs for each. The energybase.ru citation is NOT currently used as the current_ref for any P1824 worklist unit (checked against every unit's current_ref in worklist.json), so there is no live-sheet error today — but it must never be cited as a P1824 source in future work; it belongs (if anywhere) to a separate oil-pipeline row.

cross_row_leads.note: interfax.ru/russia/836081 (2022-04-21) states that at the end of 2021 ('в конце прошлого года'), Gazprom completed installation of a second string on the SKV mainline's Komsomolsk-na-Amure-Khabarovsk section (previously a smaller-diameter bottleneck than the rest of the trunk), built specifically to raise capacity ahead of phasing out the Okha-Komsomolsk gas pipeline (this row, P1824) and to serve major new loads (a GOK at the Malmyzh copper deposit in Nanaysky district, and Khabarovsk CHP-4, together >1.5 bcm/y of additional demand). If P2027 is this Komsomolsk-Khabarovsk second string (~390.8 km, completed Dec 2021 per prior research), this article independently corroborates it as a legitimate, separate capacity-expansion project on the SKV system — not a duplicate of P0758 or P1824 — built as the direct enabling predecessor to this row's planned retirement. Worth checking P2027's fills cite this article too.

The same interfax source, plus every dated source gathered for this row's status review (ng662218 2021, ng734703 2022, todaykhv 2024, nangs 2025, ng922758 2026, eastrussia 2026), consistently identifies the SKV (Sakhalin-Khabarovsk-Vladivostok) mainline as the Gazprom-owned/operated replacement capacity absorbing P1824's consumers via new branch pipes ('газопроводы-отводы') under active, multi-year construction (2023-2026+, still not complete as of 2026-04-24). If P0758 is this SKV mainline, its Capacity/Status/researcher notes may be worth cross-checking against this same reconnection-buildout evidence chain, and against the Dec-2021 Komsomolsk-Khabarovsk second-string capacity addition (see the P2027 lead above) if that capacity increment is being attributed to P0758 instead.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: ANNUAL-UPDATE STATUS REVIEW. Full evidentiary timeline assembled across 6 dated sources: 2021-01-29 (ng662218) — Gazprom board first documents the reconnection/decommission plan (contract with ExxonNeftegas/Sakhalin-1 expiring 2025 is the trigger). 2022-04-21 (interfax) — still operating at reduced pressure; decommission targeted 'after 2025'; 2023 reconnection start, 2025 completion planned; NOTES the enabling SKV second-string (Komsomolsk-Khabarovsk) completed late 2021. 2022-04-21 (ng734703) — reconnection process formally begins 2023. 2024-11-19 (todaykhv) — STILL operating; explicitly future-tense ('в ближайшее время будет выведен из эксплуатации и законсервирован' — will be taken out of service and mothballed in the near future); high district-level readiness reported. 2025 (nangs, Gazprom board report covering Jan-Apr 2025 gasification) — branch pipes ('газопроводы-отводы') for the reconnection nearing completion, launch planned summer 2025. 2026-04-24 (ng922758, MOST RECENT/MOST AUTHORITATVE — Gazprom's own board) — reconnection still described as ONGOING/present-tense ('строятся'), decommissioning still 'planned' (not executed). 2026-07-08 (eastrussia, most recent by date but a secondary/summary piece, not a primary Gazprom report) — past-tense language about the 5-year reconnection investment ('который не подлежал дальнейшей эксплуатации') could be read as suggesting near-completion, but does not explicitly state P1824 has been shut down and is less authoritative on this specific point than Gazprom's own April 2026 board report. CONCLUSION: Status=operating remains the best-supported reading of the current evidence, verdict=confirm. However this is flagged as an ACTIVE, ADVANCED, multi-year decommissioning-in-progress case, not a stable long-term operating asset — RECOMMEND a shortened recheck interval (6-12 months, watching for the SKV branch-pipe completion / formal decommission announcement) rather than the standard annual cadence.

summary: P1824 (Okha-Komsomolsk Gas Pipeline) is confirmed as a real, correctly classified, currently-operating 1987-built gas transmission trunkline (445 km / 720 mm OD / ~1 bcm/y throughput / 5.4 MPa formation pressure, no compressor stations), owned/operated 100% by Rosneft PJSC and fed by the Sakhalin-1 project -- NOT a duplicate of the SKV mainline (likely P0758) or its Dec-2021 Komsomolsk-Khabarovsk second string (likely P2027), and NOT the same asset as the older, separate Okha-Komsomolsk OIL pipeline that gem.wiki's harvested energybase.ru citation actually describes (flagged as a caveat so it is never mistakenly cited for this row). Staged REVERIFIED on 5 units (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Start, Owner) and REFS_ADDED on 6 units (Capacity, Pressure, Length, Diameter -- all single-source/medium tier from one 1995 OGJ article, second-source search documented and unsuccessful; FuelSource -- high tier, 2 independent sources; Location -- high tier, correcting non-canonical province spellings to 'Sakhalin Oblast'/'Khabarovsk Krai'; Operator -- high tier, MISSING_REF resolved). 3 units left UNRESOLVED with documented searches (Proposal, Construction, SegmentCost -- all plausibly unrecoverable for this Soviet-era asset). The most consequential finding is an ACTIVE, ADVANCED, multi-year decommissioning-in-progress trajectory (2021 plan -> 2023 reconnection start -> 2025 planned completion -> still ongoing per Gazprom's own 2026-04-24 board report): Status=operating is confirmed as correct on the best current evidence, but status_reviews[] recommends a shortened 6-12 month recheck interval given how far along the SKV reconnection buildout already is.
